extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and practitioners (applicants/attorneys) handling PCT international applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for filing, searching, examining, publishing, and entering national stage of PCT (international) patent applications, directed at USPTO examiners and practitioners. Covers Receiving Office, ISA/IPEA/IB roles, time limits, required documents, amendment options, and differences between national and national-stage filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic PCT filing concept
rubrics_metrics.description: File one international application in a standardized format in a Receiving Office and have that application acknowledged as a regular national or regional filing in as many Contracting States as the applicant designates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing of an international application will automatically constitute the designation of all contracting countries to the PCT on that filing date. The PCT provides for establishment of an international search report and written opinion at 16 months and publication after 18 months; national stage procedures follow usually 30 months after priority or international filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiving Office competence and role
rubrics_metrics.description: International applications must be filed in the prescribed Receiving Office (RO); the RO acts as the filing and formalities review organization and must meet standards for completeness and formality (PCT Articles 11(1) and 14(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO acts as RO for U.S. residents/nationals; the IB may also act as RO. The RO grants an international filing date, collects fees, handles informalities by direct communication with the applicant, monitors corrections, prepares/transmits the search copy (SC) to the ISA by 13 months from priority date, forwards record copy (RC) to IB, and retains home copy (HC). Where the RO is not competent (e.g., language or residence issues), the application may be forwarded to the IB as RO under PCT Rule 19.4.

rubrics_metrics.name: International filing date requirements (Article 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain an international filing date the international application must satisfy Article 11 requirements (include a description, a claim, names at least one applicant who is a resident or national of a PCT Contracting State, be filed in a prescribed language, and designate at least one Contracting State).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The international filing date is used for timing international processing, transmittals, payment of fees, and publication. If no priority is claimed, the international filing date is treated as the priority date (PCT Article 2(xi)). See MPEP § 1810 for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of required fees to obtain processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain fees for the international application are payable within one month from the date of receipt of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See PCT Rules 14.1(c), 15.3, and 16.1(f). The RO will collect fees as part of granting an international filing date and processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim timing and documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a priority claim is made, the earliest-filed application whose priority is claimed is used as the priority date for international processing; if no priority claim is made, the international filing date is used as the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a certified copy of the priority document is not filed with the RO, the applicant must submit it directly to the IB or RO not later than 16 months after the priority date (PCT Rule 17). The RO or IB can be requested to obtain and transmit copies if available in digital libraries (Form PCT/RO/101).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal of search copy to ISA
rubrics_metrics.description: By 13 months from the priority date, the Receiving Office should prepare and transmit the search copy to the International Searching Authority (ISA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This transmittal obligation is under PCT Rules 22.1 and 23; timely transmittal focuses international processing on the ISA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice and competence of International Searching Authority (ISA)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed with the U.S. Receiving Office, applicant may choose among specified ISAs (e.g., USPTO, EPO, KIPO, IP Australia, ILPO, JPO, IPOS), but some ISAs may not be competent for certain applications filed by nationals/residents of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 1840.01-1840.07. The ISA is responsible for minimum documentation searches and checking title and abstract (PCT Rules 34, 37.2, and 38.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: International Search Report (ISR) timing and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISA normally issues an international search report (ISR) listing documents found to be relevant and identifying the claims to which they are pertinent, normally within 3 months from receipt of the search copy (about 16 months from priority date) (PCT Rule 42).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of the ISR and cited prior art are made available to applicant and IB (PCT Rules 43 and 44.1). The ISR identifies relevant documents and which claims they pertain to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written Opinion of the ISA — substantive criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The written opinion indicates whether each claim appears to satisfy PCT Article 33 criteria of novelty, inventive step, and industrial applicability, and may indicate defects in form or content (clarity, description support, drawings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written opinion (PCT Rule 43 bis) normally accompanies the ISR and may be considered the first written opinion of the IPEA. It may also note defects the ISA wishes to make on clarity and support of claims/description/drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant right to amend claims under Article 19
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant ordinarily has 2 months from transmittal of the international search report to amend the claims by filing an Article 19 amendment and may file a brief statement explaining the amendment directly with the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See PCT Article 19 and PCT Rule 46. Any Article 19 amendments are normally published with the international application at 18 months along with the search report.

rubrics_metrics.name: International publication timing and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau normally publishes the international application along with the search report and any amended claims at the expiration of 18 months from the priority date (PCT Article 21).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication includes a front page with bibliographical data, the abstract, and a figure of the drawing (PCT Rule 48). For applications filed on or after July 1, 2014, the written opinion of the ISA and applicant's informal comments are made public in their original language as of publication date. If published in a language other than English, the search report and abstract are also published in English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated and elected offices; national stage entry timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated Offices are those named under Chapter I; elected Offices are those elected under Chapter II. Copies, translations, and national fees are due to a designated Office not later than 30 months from the priority date (PCT Article 22(1) as amended).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most Contracting States adopted the 30-month limit; exceptions (states that did not adopt Article 22(1) as amended) may require different deadlines (e.g., Luxembourg, United Republic of Tanzania). To delay entry into national stage to 30 months in such states, filing a Demand for Chapter II within 19 months can extend national-stage entry to 30 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing to file Demand for international preliminary examination (Chapter II)
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT Rule 54 bis.1 requires the Demand to be made prior to the expiration of whichever of the following periods expires later: (A) three months from transmittal of the ISR and written opinion, or (B) 22 months from the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, applicants may file the Demand by 19 months to extend the national stage entry deadline in certain countries (e.g., Luxembourg and Tanzania). The Demand must also elect those states in which Chapter II is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPEA start conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA normally starts examination when it is in possession of: (A) the Demand, (B) the amount due, (C) a translation if required under PCT Rule 55.2, (D) either the ISR or a notice that no ISR will be established, and (E) the written opinion established under PCT Rule 43 bis.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IPEA shall start examination upon receipt unless applicant requests postponement until the later of three months from transmittal or 22 months from priority date, subject to exceptions in PCT Rule 69.1(b)-(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: International Preliminary Report on Patentability (IPRP) timing and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA establishes the international preliminary examination report (international preliminary report on patentability) presenting the examiner’s final position on whether each claim is novel, involves inventive step, and is industrially applicable by 28 months from the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the report is sent to the applicant and the International Bureau, which communicates it to elected Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written Opinion treatment in Chapter II
rubrics_metrics.description: The written opinion of the ISA is usually considered the first written opinion of the IPEA unless the IPEA has notified IB that written opinions established by specified ISAs shall not be considered for this purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IPEA may, at its discretion, issue further written opinions if time permits (PCT Rule 66.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: International Bureau (IB) functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The IB maintains the master file of all international applications, acts as publisher and central coordinating body under the Treaty, and communicates publications and reports to designated/elected Offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IB also handles requests to obtain priority documents from digital libraries and publishes the PCT Gazette. It transmits publications to designated Offices that have requested to receive them (PCT Article 20, Rules 47, 86).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority document submission and retrieval
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant has not filed a certified copy of the priority document with the RO, the applicant must submit it to the IB or RO not later than 16 months after the priority date; the RO or IB can be requested to obtain copies from digital libraries when available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PCT/RO/101 contains boxes to request RO prepare/transmit a copy of the prior national application or request the IB to obtain a copy from a digital library (subject to availability and access codes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Facsimile transmission limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Facsimile transmission (without certificate under 37 CFR 1.8(a)) may be used to submit certain papers but may not be used for filing an international application, filing color drawings, or filing the copy of the international application and basic national fee to enter the U.S. national stage; the Demand may be filed by facsimile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.6(d)(3) and (4), 1.8(a)(2)(i)(D) and (F). Receipt date rules under 37 CFR 1.6 and Priority Mail Express® under 37 CFR 1.10 apply; PCT international applications are excluded from Certificate of Mailing/Transmission under 37 CFR 1.8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file in the U.S. Receiving Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Only if at least one of the applicants is a resident or national of the United States may an international application be filed in the United States Receiving Office (35 U.S.C. 361; PCT Article 9; PCT Rule 18).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Residence and nationality concepts are defined in PCT Rule 18.1. An applicant may also file directly with the IB as RO if eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forwarding to IB as Receiving Office (PCT Rule 19.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the U.S. RO is not competent (e.g., language not accepted or applicant lacks requisite residence/nationality), PCT Rule 19.4 provides for transmittal of the application to the IB to act as Receiving Office; the IB will consider the application received as of the date accorded by the U.S. RO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice avoids loss of filing date when the U.S. RO is not competent but the application indicates nationality/residence of a Contracting State or is in a language accepted by IB as RO. If no residence/nationality is indicated, the U.S. is not competent and the application will be forwarded to the IB as RO if the necessary fee is paid (transmittal fee).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign filing license requirements for IB-filed applications
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application filed with or forwarded to the IB must have a foreign filing license unless: (1) the invention was not made in the United States; or (2) a U.S. national application on the invention was filed at least six months prior, is not subject to a secrecy order, and the international application does not contain amendments changing the general nature of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 5.11 and 5.15 for foreign filing license rules and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicants and inventors — who may be applicant and inventor indications
rubrics_metrics.description: Any resident or national of a Contracting State may file an international application; the applicant can be an individual, corporate entity, or other concern. Where inventor is not applicant, indications concerning the inventor must be made in the Request when required by national law of designated States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inventor only is to be indicated, mark 'inventor only' box, indicate name and address in Box III, and omit inventor residence and nationality when appropriate. See PCT Applicant’s Guide Annexes for states requiring inventor information at filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for continuations/divisional/continuation-in-part (bypass) to obtain benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120/365(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 and 365(c) of a prior international application designating the U.S., a continuing application must: (A) include a specific reference to the prior international application, (B) be copending with the prior international application, and (C) have at least one inventor in common with the prior international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If continuing application filed prior to Sept 16, 2012, the specific reference must be in first sentences of the specification following the title or in an application data sheet; if filed on/after Sept 16, 2012, the reference must be in an application data sheet (37 CFR 1.78(d)(2)). The specific reference must identify the international application number, filing date, and relationship (continuation, division, CIP). The reference must be submitted within the time in 37 CFR 1.78(d)(3) (non-extendable). A certified copy of the international application and/or translation may be required to perfect benefit if necessary (e.g., intervening reference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copendency and abandonment rules for benefit claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A U.S. national application is copending with a prior international application if the international application was pending on the filing date of the U.S. national application. An international application generally becomes abandoned as to the U.S. upon expiration of 30 months from the priority date unless a proper submission under 35 U.S.C. 371 to enter national phase is filed prior to expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special rules applied to pre-April 1, 2002 filings where 20/19 month deadlines applied. Examiners may require inspection of home copy or applicant certification that international application was not withdrawn. If parent international application was not copending (abandoned/withdrawn), benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 is not possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differences between 35 U.S.C. 111(a) national applications and 35 U.S.C. 371 national-stage applications
rubrics_metrics.description: There are differences in filing date determination, priority claim procedures and timing, unity of invention/restriction practice, and fee regimes between a U.S. national application under 111(a) and a national-stage application under 371.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: filing date for 111(a) is when a specification is received (37 CFR 1.53(b)), whereas national-stage uses the international filing date; priority document submission rules differ (37 CFR 1.55(f)(1) vs 1.55(f)(2)); unity/restriction practice follows 37 CFR 1.141-1.146 for 111(a) but unity under 1.475/1.499 for national-stage; fees differ (37 CFR 1.16 vs 1.492).

rubrics_metrics.name: International Search/Written Opinion public availability changes (post-2014)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after July 1, 2014, the written opinion of the ISA and any informal comments submitted by the applicant are made available to the public in their original language as of the publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For earlier applications, the written opinion was not publicly available until 30 months under former PCT Rule 44ter. The IB publishes these materials along with the international application front page and search report.
